title: Solving modulo a power of q by an essentially smooth Artinian algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $\Lambda$ a Noetherian $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which is geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$ a prime ideal, $n\ge1$ an integer and $E\subset\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ a finite subset ($\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ the localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]). Then there are an integer $m\ge0$ and a homomorphism of $k$-algebras $\varphi:k[y_1,\dots,y_m]\to\Lambda$ with the following properties, where $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ and $P=k[y_1,\dots,y_m]_{\mathfrak p}$: (1) $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak p\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ and the induced map $P\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; (2) there is a factorization $P/\mathfrak p^nP\to D\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ of the induced map by local homomorphisms of local Artinian rings, where the first arrow is essentially smooth [def-weil-pbc-essentially-smooth-ring-map] and the second is flat; (3) every element of $E$ lies in the image of $D\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, line 2552), Section 07FF; its proof uses Lemma Tag 07FG (lemma-helper)

proof.text: *Setup.* $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ and residue field $K=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], Noetherian as a localization of the Noetherian ring $\Lambda$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], and $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\cap\Lambda=\mathfrak q$. It is geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]: for a finite purely inseparable $k'/k$, $k'\otimes_k\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is the localization of the regular ring $k'\otimes_k\Lambda$ at the image of $\Lambda\setminus\mathfrak q$ (tensor products commute with localization), hence regular [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-regular-ring]. Set $\bar\Lambda=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ (Stacks' notation); it is an Artinian local $k$-algebra with maximal ideal $\bar{\mathfrak m}=\mathfrak q\bar\Lambda$, $\bar{\mathfrak m}^n=0$, and residue field $K$ [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, lines 2575-2623): 'Set Lambda-bar = Lambda_q/q^n Lambda_q'

proof.text: *$\dim_KH_1(L_{K/k})<\infty$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-h1-injective] applied to the Noetherian local $k$-algebra $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, geometrically regular over $k$ (step 1), the canonical map $H_1(L_{K/k})\to\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q^2\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] is injective. The target is a finite dimensional $K$-vector space, since the ideal $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ of the Noetherian ring $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is finitely generated. Hence $H_1(L_{K/k})$ is finite dimensional.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, lines 2575-2623): 'Note that dim H_1(L_{kappa(q)/k}) < infinity by More on Algebra, Proposition 07E5'

proof.text: *A first subring $A_0\supseteq E$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-artinian-flat-subalgebras] (Stacks 07FG) applied to the Artinian local $k$-algebra $\bar\Lambda$ with residue field $K$ (steps 1, 2), $\bar\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of Artinian local $k$-algebras $A_i$, essentially of finite type over $k$, with flat maps $A_i\to\bar\Lambda$ and $\mathfrak m_{A_i}\bar\Lambda=\bar{\mathfrak m}$. Each $A_i\to\bar\Lambda$ maps $\mathfrak m_{A_i}$ into $\bar{\mathfrak m}$, so it is a flat local homomorphism, hence faithfully flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat] and injective [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] ($I=0$); identify $A_i$ with its image, a $k$-subalgebra of $\bar\Lambda$, flat over $A_i$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Every element of $\bar\Lambda$ lies in some $A_i$ and the system is filtered, so the finite set $E$ lies in one of them, $A_0$. In the terminology of [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-solution-modulo-choose], $A_0$ is admissible.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, lines 2575-2623): 'Pick A in Lambda-bar containing E such that A is local Artinian, essentially of finite type over k, the map A -> Lambda-bar is flat, and m_A generates the maximal ideal of Lambda-bar, see Lemma 07FG'

proof.text: *The subring $A$ and the elements $\lambda$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-solution-modulo-choose] applied to $A_0$ there are an admissible $A\subseteq\bar\Lambda$ with $E\subseteq A_0\subseteq A$, residue field $F=A/\mathfrak m_A$ with $k\subseteq F\subseteq K$, elements $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_t\in\Lambda$ whose images in $\bar\Lambda$ lie in $A$ and whose residues $\bar\lambda_j\in F$ have differentials $\mathrm d\bar\lambda_1,\dots,\mathrm d\bar\lambda_t$ forming a basis of $\Omega_{F/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and elements $\lambda'_1,\dots,\lambda'_r\in\mathfrak q$ with images in $A$ which generate $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$. Since $A$ is essentially of finite type over $k$, so is its quotient field $F$, which is therefore a finitely generated field extension of $k$ (generated by the images of finitely many algebra generators). (Stacks picks the $\lambda_j$ for the subring of step 3 directly; as recorded in [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-solution-modulo-choose], that is not possible for every such subring, which is why $A_0$ is enlarged.)

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, lines 2575-2623): 'Denote F = A/m_A the residue field so that k in F in K. Pick lambda_1,...,lambda_t in Lambda which map to elements of A in Lambda-bar such that moreover the images of d lambda_1,...,d lambda_t form a basis of Omega_{F/k}'

proof.text: *Flatness of the first part.* Let $\varphi':k[y_1,\dots,y_t]\to\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] send $y_j\mapsto\lambda_j$ and $\mathfrak p'=(\varphi')^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$; since $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\cap\Lambda=\mathfrak q$, $\mathfrak p'$ is also the inverse image of the maximal ideal under $k[y_1,\dots,y_t]\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-over-field-flat] (Stacks 07E6) to the Noetherian local $k$-algebra $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, geometrically regular over $k$ (step 1), the finitely generated subextension $k\subseteq F\subseteq K$ and this map (the image of $y_j$ in $K$ is $\bar\lambda_j\in F$, and the $\mathrm d\bar\lambda_j$ form a basis of $\Omega_{F/k}$, step 4): $P'=k[y_1,\dots,y_t]_{\mathfrak p'}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $S:=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak p'\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], with maximal ideal $\mathfrak qS$ and residue field $K$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, lines 2575-2623): 'Consider the map phi': k[y_1..y_t] -> Lambda ... By More on Algebra, Lemma 07E6 the ring map k[y_1..y_t]_{p'} -> Lambda_q is flat and Lambda_q/p'Lambda_q is regular'

proof.text: *A regular system of parameters of $S$ from the $\lambda'_i$.* The images of $\lambda'_1,\dots,\lambda'_r$ generate $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ (step 4), hence the maximal ideal $\mathfrak qS$ of $S$, hence span the $K$-vector space $\mathfrak qS/\mathfrak q^2S$. Choose among them $e$ elements whose images form a basis of $\mathfrak qS/\mathfrak q^2S$ and call them $\lambda_{t+1},\dots,\lambda_m$ ($m=t+e$). By Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] their images generate $\mathfrak qS$, and no proper subset does, so they form a minimal set of generators of the maximal ideal of the regular local ring $S$, i.e. a regular system of parameters, and $e=\dim S$ [def-weil-regular-scheme] [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence]. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] their images form a regular sequence in $S$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and $S/(\lambda_{t+1},\dots,\lambda_m)S=S/\mathfrak qS=K\ne0$. Each $\lambda_{t+i}$ lies in $\mathfrak q$ and its image in $\bar\Lambda$ lies in $A$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, lines 2575-2623): 'Thus we can choose further elements lambda_{t+1},...,lambda_m in Lambda which map into A in Lambda-bar and which map to a regular system of parameters of Lambda_q/p'Lambda_q'

proof.text: *The map $\varphi$ and $\mathfrak p\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$.* Let $\varphi:k[y_1,\dots,y_m]\to\Lambda$, $y_j\mapsto\lambda_j$, extend $\varphi'$, $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ and $P=k[y_1,\dots,y_m]_{\mathfrak p}$. Then $\mathfrak p\cap k[y_1,\dots,y_t]=\mathfrak p'$ and $y_{t+1},\dots,y_m\in\mathfrak p$ (as $\lambda_{t+i}\in\mathfrak q$). Since $\varphi(\mathfrak p)\subseteq\mathfrak q$, $\mathfrak p\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\subseteq\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$; conversely $\mathfrak p\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\supseteq\mathfrak p'\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}+(\lambda_{t+1},\dots,\lambda_m)\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, which is all of $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ because the images of $\lambda_{t+1},\dots,\lambda_m$ generate $\mathfrak qS=\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak p'\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ (step 6). So $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak p\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, the first half of (1).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, lines 2575-2623): 'We obtain phi: k[y_1..y_m] -> Lambda having property (1)'

proof.text: *The closed fibre $P/\mathfrak p'P$.* Elements of $k[y_1,\dots,y_t]\setminus\mathfrak p'$ are not in $\mathfrak p$, so they are units of $P$; hence $P/\mathfrak p'P$ is the localization of $\kappa(\mathfrak p')[y_{t+1},\dots,y_m]$ ($\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ the fraction field of $k[y_1,\dots,y_t]/\mathfrak p'$) at the image $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ of $\mathfrak p$. As $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ contains the maximal ideal $(y_{t+1},\dots,y_m)$ (step 7) and is proper, it equals it. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-origin-regular-local] over the field $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$, $P/\mathfrak p'P$ is a regular local ring of dimension $e=m-t$ whose maximal ideal is generated by $y_{t+1},\dots,y_m$. $P'$, $P$ are Noetherian local rings (localizations [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] of polynomial rings over a field [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]), and $P'\to P$ (localization of the inclusion, $\mathfrak p\cap k[y_1,\dots,y_t]=\mathfrak p'$) and $P\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ are local homomorphisms, with $\mathfrak m_{P'}P=\mathfrak p'P$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, lines 2575-2623) (the flatness in property (1), left implicit by Stacks; it repeats the end of the proof of More on Algebra, Lemma 07E6)

proof.text: *$P\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat.* The induced local homomorphism $P/\mathfrak p'P\to S=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak p'\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ of Noetherian local rings sends the regular system of parameters $y_{t+1},\dots,y_m$ of the regular local ring $P/\mathfrak p'P$ (step 8) to $\lambda_{t+1},\dots,\lambda_m$, a regular sequence in $S$ with nonzero quotient (step 6); so it is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular] (Algebra 07DY). Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-criterion-flatness-fibre-noetherian] (Algebra 00MP) to $P'\to P\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ and $M=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$: these are Noetherian local rings and local homomorphisms (steps 1, 8); $M$ is generated by $1$ and nonzero; $M/\mathfrak m_{P'}M=S$ is flat over $P/\mathfrak m_{P'}P=P/\mathfrak p'P$ (just shown); $M$ is flat over $P'$ (step 5). Hence $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $P$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. With step 7 this proves (1).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, lines 2575-2623): 'We obtain phi having property (1)'; More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 07E6 (line 8885: 'We win by Algebra, Lemmas 00R4 and 00NQ')

proof.text: *The factorization through $A$.* Write $\bar P=P/\mathfrak p^nP$, an Artinian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak p\bar P$ and residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local]. The images of $y_1,\dots,y_m$ in $\bar\Lambda$ lie in $A$ (steps 4, 6), so $k[y_1,\dots,y_m]\to\bar\Lambda$ takes values in $A$. An element $g\notin\mathfrak p$ maps to an element of $A$ outside $\bar{\mathfrak m}$, i.e. outside $\mathfrak m_A=A\cap\bar{\mathfrak m}$, hence to a unit of the local ring $A$; by the universal property of localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] $k[y]\to A$ extends to $P\to A$, which composed with $A\subseteq\bar\Lambda$ is $P\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\to\bar\Lambda$. The latter kills $\mathfrak p^nP$ (it maps into $\mathfrak q^n\bar\Lambda=0$) and $A\subseteq\bar\Lambda$ is injective, so we get $\bar P\to A\to\bar\Lambda$, local homomorphisms of local Artinian rings ($\mathfrak p$ maps into $\mathfrak m_A$). Put $D=A$. Then $D\to\bar\Lambda$ is flat ($A$ admissible) and $E\subseteq A_0\subseteq D$, which is (3).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, lines 2575-2623): 'such that k[y_1..y_m]_p/p^n k[y_1..y_m]_p -> Lambda-bar factors through A'

proof.text: *$\bar P\to A$ is flat.* Since $\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak p^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ (step 7), $\bar\Lambda=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_P\bar P$, which is flat over $\bar P$ by base change of the flat $P$-module $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ (step 9) [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change]. The flat local homomorphism $A\to\bar\Lambda$ is faithfully flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat]. So the $A$-module $\bar\Lambda$ is flat over $\bar P$ and faithfully flat over $A$, and $\bar P\to A$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-permanence] (Stacks cites Algebra 0584 (2) with $S=A$, $S'=\bar\Lambda$, $M=A$, which is this instance).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, lines 2575-2623): 'Thus k[y]_p/p^n -> A is flat by Algebra, Lemma 0584'

proof.text: *$\mathfrak m_A=\mathfrak pA$.* By step 7, $(\mathfrak pA)\bar\Lambda=\mathfrak p\bar\Lambda=\mathfrak q\bar\Lambda=\bar{\mathfrak m}=\mathfrak m_A\bar\Lambda$. Since $A\to\bar\Lambda$ is faithfully flat (step 11), [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] gives $\mathfrak m_A\subseteq\mathfrak m_A\bar\Lambda\cap A=(\mathfrak pA)\bar\Lambda\cap A=\mathfrak pA\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$. So the maximal ideal of $\bar P$ generates the maximal ideal of $A$ (needed for the étaleness criterion below; Stacks leaves it implicit).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, lines 2575-2623) (condition (3) of Algebra, Lemma 00U6, left implicit)

proof.text: *$F/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is finite separable.* The local map $\bar P\to A$ induces $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to F$, and $F$ is finitely generated over $k$ (step 4), hence over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. The universal derivation $F\to\Omega_{F/\kappa(\mathfrak p)}$ is a $k$-derivation, so by the universal property [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] there is an $F$-linear map $\Omega_{F/k}\to\Omega_{F/\kappa(\mathfrak p)}$, $\mathrm df\mapsto\mathrm df$, which is surjective (the $\mathrm df$ generate). It kills $\mathrm d\bar\lambda_j$ for $j\le t$, since $\bar\lambda_j$ is the image of $y_j\in\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $\mathrm d$ vanishes on $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$; these span $\Omega_{F/k}$ (step 4). Hence $\Omega_{F/\kappa(\mathfrak p)}=0$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-fg-field-zero-differentials-separable] $F/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is finite and separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, lines 2575-2623): 'By construction the residue field extension F/kappa(p) is finitely generated and Omega_{F/kappa(p)} = 0. Hence it is finite separable by More on Algebra, Lemma 07E1' (the separability is Algebra, Lemma 090W (2)=>(1))

proof.text: *$\bar P\to A$ is finite and finitely presented.* $A$ is Artinian with Jacobson radical $\mathfrak m_A$ and $A/\mathfrak m_A=F$ is a finite $\bar P$-module (finite over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, step 13, and $\bar P\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is surjective); so $A$ is a finite $\bar P$-module [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-finite-over-residue-finite], in particular a $\bar P$-algebra of finite type. $\bar P$ is Noetherian (a quotient of the Noetherian ring $P$), so $A$ is finitely presented over $\bar P$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, lines 2575-2623): 'Thus k[y]_p/p^n -> A is finite by Algebra, Lemma 07DT'

proof.text: *$\bar P\to D=A$ is étale, hence essentially smooth.* By [lem-weil-pbc-local-flat-unramified-etale] (Algebra 00U6, local case) applied to the local homomorphism $\bar P\to A$: finitely presented (step 14), flat (step 11), $\mathfrak m_{\bar P}A=\mathfrak m_A$ (step 12), residue extension finite separable (step 13); so $\bar P\to A$ is étale in the sense of Algebra 00U1, equivalently $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}\bar P$ is étale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine]. By remark (a) of [def-weil-pbc-essentially-smooth-ring-map] an étale ring map is essentially smooth. Together with step 10 this is (2).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, lines 2575-2623): 'Finally, we conclude that it is etale by Algebra, Lemma 00U6. Since an etale ring map is certainly essentially smooth we win.'

split_report.summary: Proof written in 15 steps following the Stacks proof of 07FH: geometric regularity of Lambda_q (localization), dim H_1(L_{K/k}) finite via 07E5 (1)=>(3) [new node], A_0 containing E via 07FG [new node], the choice of A and of lambda_1..lambda_m [new node -choose], flatness of k[y_1..y_t]_{p'} -> Lambda_q and regularity of the fibre via 07E6 [new node], selection of a regular system of parameters (Nakayama), pLambda_q = qLambda_q, flatness of P -> Lambda_q (07DY on the closed fibre, then 00MP; Stacks leaves it implicit), the factorization through A, flatness of P/p^n -> A (Stacks cites 0584; the instance used is 039V, existing node), m_A = pA by faithful flatness (implicit in Stacks, needed for 00U6), F/kappa(p) finite separable (Stacks cites Cartier 07E1; the precise statement is 090W (2)=>(1), new Mathlib leaf), finiteness via 07DT (existing leaf for Artinian rings), etale via 00U6 local case (new Mathlib leaf), essentially smooth by remark (a) of the definition. Gap in Stacks: 'Pick lambda_1..lambda_t in Lambda which map to elements of A' fails for some A allowed by 07FG (Lambda=k[x,y], q=0, n=1, A=k(x/y): k[x,y] meets k(x/y) only in k); the choice is a separate node whose statement lets A be enlarged, with a proof sketch via the three cases of 07FI recorded in its source. Statement and stmt_deps kept.
